title: Simultaneous pointed affine strict-local chart models
statement: Let $i:Z\to W$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field and $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $j:\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$ and $k:\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to Z$ be open immersions whose square with $i$ and the quotient spectrum map is cartesian [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose that the composite point in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the point of a prime $p$ with its specified embedding $\kappa(p)\to\Omega$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Put $R=A_p$, $S=R/IR$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $K=\operatorname{separableClosure}(\kappa(p),\Omega)$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure], $C=\mathcal O^{sh}_{W,i(kx)}$ and $D=\mathcal O^{sh}_{Z,kx}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with their specified evaluations to $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-point-evaluation]. There are chart maps $\alpha:A\to C$, $\beta:A/I\to D$ factoring their structural morphisms through $j,k$. The ring $S$ is local and is a localization of $A/I$ at the image of $A\setminus p$, compatibly with $R\to S$. There are local base maps $R\to C$, $S\to D$ extending $\alpha,\beta$, compatible actions of $R,S$ on the same $K$, each factoring through its residue field, and specified pointed-etale colimit presentations of $C,D$ over these bases [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Both rings are strictly henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Their residue-field identifications with $K$ are induced by the specified presentations, their composites into $\Omega$ are exactly the geometric evaluations, and their base restrictions are the specified base maps to $K$. No assertion about a map $C\to D$ or the quotient $C/IC$ is part of this statement.

proof.text: The specified geometric point has ambient prime p containing I. Its quotient prime is p/I. Localizing A/I at this prime gives S=R/IR: the images of elements outside p are units, and the quotient and localization universal properties give mutually inverse homomorphisms. This gives the chart equation and the localization instance for S. The local quotient R to S identifies residue fields. Transport the separable closure K and its residue embedding through that identification; the resulting actions of R and S on K agree through R to S.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] to the local rings $R$ and $S$, their maximal ideals and the specified common separable closure $K$ (a separable closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure], $\Omega$ being algebraically closed). Its index category is the pair category of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]: an etale algebra map $\chi:S'\to K$ over a local base determines the triple $(S',\ker\chi,\kappa(\ker\chi)\to K)$, where $\ker\chi$ lies over the maximal ideal because the base maps to $K$ through its residue field, and conversely $\phi$ gives $\chi$ as the composite $S'\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to K$; morphisms correspond, since $\chi'\beta=\chi$ forces $\beta^{-1}(\ker\chi')=\ker\chi$ and $\phi'\kappa(\beta)=\phi$. So the triple colimits are algebraic strict henselizations relative to $K$. Apply [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] to $U\hookrightarrow W$ at $i\bar a$, and to $i^{-1}(U)\hookrightarrow Z$ at $\bar a$, using these algebraic models. Its structure-map equation gives the asserted factorizations through the two affine opens, the chart maps $A\to C$ and $A/I\to D$ being the colimit legs (as $\theta$ is an algebra isomorphism over the chart ring). Every $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ becomes a unit in $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, hence in $C$ via $\theta^{-1}$, so [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] extends $A\to C$ uniquely to $R\to C$, and likewise $A/I\to D$ to $S\to D$; by the same uniqueness $\theta$ is an isomorphism of $R$- (respectively $S$-)algebras. Hence $C$ and $D$ are algebraic strict henselizations of $R$ and $S$ relative to $K$, transporting the defining universal cocones as in [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Its evaluation equation identifies both geometric residue fields with the specified $K$, and both rings are strictly henselian local. The maps $R\to C$ and $S\to D$ are local: their composites to $K$ are the residue maps followed by the specified residue-field embeddings, whose kernels are precisely the maximal ideals of $R$ and $S$. For this lemma stop before comparing any canonical map between C and D. Transport the universal cocones, local structures and residue isomorphisms across the two pointed affine comparisons. The base maps are local because the composite to K is the residue embedding, whose kernel is the base maximal ideal.
